question: A plane wavefront travelling in air is incident on glass. If the speed of light in glass is less than that in air, will the refracted ray bend towards or away from the normal? Justify your answer.

options.A: In glass, light speed is lower than in air, so $v_2<v_1$. Hence $\dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r}=\dfrac{v_1}{v_2}>1$, which gives $i>r$. The refracted ray bends towards the normal.
options.B: The ray bends away from the normal because the wavelength becomes shorter in glass.
options.C: The ray remains undeviated because frequency does not change.
options.D: The refracted ray bends away from the normal because $v_2<v_1$.
